The engine emits **only what changed** relative to its previous emission:

each frame as a delta to its native elements.

1: //! The fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode.
2: //!
3: //! Layout (see `spec/OPCODE.md`):
4: //!
5: //! ```text
6: //! [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
7: //! ```
8: //!
9: //! All multi-byte fields are little-endian on the wire. `size_of::<Opcode>() == 16`,
10: //! so a 64-byte cache line holds exactly 4 opcodes.

18: ///
19: /// This struct intentionally mirrors the wire layout and is `#[repr(C, packed)]`
20: /// per the specification. Because it is packed, fields may be unaligned; always
21: /// read fields through the accessor methods (which use unaligned reads) rather
22: /// than by value.
23: #[repr(C, packed)]
24: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
25: pub struct Opcode {
26:     /// Opcode category (see `constants::Category`).

28:     /// Command within the category (see `constants::Command*`).

1: //! # pathland-engine
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland **guest engine**. It holds the application's **retained view
4: //! tree** and emits the **declarative structure** as `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes into
5: //! the 16-byte ring buffer — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment.
6: //! It does **not** compute rects or layout; native renderers (GTK4 widgets,
7: //! DOM flexbox) lay out their own native elements from these constraints.
8: //!
9: //! ## Reactive emission
10: //!
11: //! Emission is **diff-based**: on each `emit` the engine compares the current
12: //! tree against a snapshot of what it last emitted, and writes only the
13: //! opcodes for nodes that actually changed. An unchanged tree emits **zero**
14: //! opcodes. This is what signals in the application drive — a signal marks the
15: //! tree dirty; `emit` reconciles.
16: //!
17: //! Both **property diffs** (`SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_TEXT`) and **structural diffs**
18: //! (`CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`, `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD`)
19: //! are emitted.
20: //!
21: //! ## Zero allocation
22: //!
23: //! The emit pass performs **zero dynamic heap allocations** in the steady
24: //! state. The snapshot is a preallocated slab indexed by node id; per-pass
25: //! bookkeeping uses generation stamps instead of rebuilding maps. Allocations
26: //! only occur when the tree *grows* (new nodes resize the slab) or a node's
27: //! property set actually changes.
28:

55:     pub id: u32,
56:     pub component: Component,
57:     pub children: Vec<Node>,

176:         }
177:     }

179:     /// Reconcile `root` against the snapshot, emitting only changed opcodes.
180:     pub fn emit(
181:         &mut self,
182:         root: &Node,
183:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
184:     ) -> Result<EmitResult, pathland_opcode::RingError> {
185:         self.gen = self.gen.wrapping_add(1);
186:         let mut out = 0usize;

228:             Component::Text { text } => (Some(text.as_str()), None, None),

238:             None => !node.properties.is_empty(),

241:         let text_changed = match &prev {

54: impl RenderTree {
55:     /// Apply a frame's opcodes to this tree (a delta).
56:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
57:         for op in frame.opcodes() {
58:             match (op.category(), op.command()) {
59:                 (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
60:                     let id = op.a();
61:                     let ty = op.b() as u16;
62:                     let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_default();
63:                     entry.id = id;
64:                     entry.component_type = ty;
65:                 }
66:                 (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => {
67:                     self.nodes.remove(&op.a());
68:                 }
69:                 (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => {
70:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
71:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
72:                         if !p.children.contains(&child) {
73:                             p.children.push(child);
74:                         }
75:                     }
76:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
77:                         c.parent = Some(parent);
78:                     }
79:                 }
80:                 (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
81:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
82:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
83:                         p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
84:                     }
85:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
86:                         c.parent = None;
87:                     }
88:                 }
89:                 (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => {
90:                     let (parent, child, new_index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c() as usize);
91:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
92:                         if let Some(pos) = p.children.iter().position(|c| *c == child) {
93:                             p.children.remove(pos);
94:                         }
95:                         let idx = if new_index == usize::MAX {
96:                             p.children.len()
97:                         } else {
98:                             new_index.min(p.children.len())
99:                         };
100:                         p.children.insert(idx, child);
101:                     }
102:                 }
103:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_PROPERTY) => {
104:                     let prop_id = op.b() as u16;
105:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
106:                         n.properties.insert(prop_id, op.c());
107:                     }
108:                 }
109:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_TEXT) => {
110:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
111:                         n.text = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok().map(|s| s.to_string());
112:                     }
113:                 }
114:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
115:                     // Token overrides are handled by the renderer's theme layer.
116:                     let _ = op;
117:                 }
118:                 _ => {}

120:         }

The vectors are enforced by the reference Rust encoder (`pathland-opcode`,

## Opcode Layout

```
[Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
```

All multi-byte fields little-endian. `A`/`B`/`C` may carry `f32` bit patterns.

## Vectors

### 1. TREE:CREATE_NODE (id=1, VSTACK=0x0002)

```

- `01` command = CREATE_NODE
- `00 00` flags = 0

- `02 00 00 00` B = componentType = 0x0002 (VSTACK)
- `00 00 00 00` C = 0

## Goal

Build the fixed-size **16-byte opcode engine** — the foundational protocol layer for the Pathland Rust core. All layout math, tree bounds, and drawing instructions are emitted by the WASM guest engine into a contiguous, fixed 16-byte opcode ring buffer in linear memory.

This is the foundation of the new Rust-first architecture (see `AGENTS.md`). Blocks Goals 2–5.

## Scope

New Rust workspace `lib/rust/`, crate `pathland-opcode` (and the `pathland-layout` layout engine hook that emits into it):

- **Opcode struct**: `#[repr(C, packed)]` — `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | Payload A (4B) | Payload B (4B) | Payload C (4B)` = exactly 16 bytes, little-endian, L1 cache-line aligned (64B line = 4 opcodes).
- **Categories / command tables**: TREE, LAYOUT, STYLE/DRAW, DRAW, EVENT, GESTURE, META. Includes `LAYOUT_SET_ORIGIN` (`nodeId, x, y`) + `LAYOUT_SET_SIZE` (`nodeId, w, h`) split-bounds opcodes.
- **Ring buffer**: contiguous power-of-two slot array; single-producer (guest engine) / single-consumer (host renderer), lock-free via `read`/`write` cursors + monotonic **frame counter** in a fixed header block. Host detects completed frames by watching the write cursor + frame counter.
- **Arena for variable-length data**: bump arena region in linear memory for strings, token paths, and child-id lists; opcodes reference it via `(offset, byteLength)` packed into A/B/C so every opcode stays 16 bytes.
- **Fixed linear-memory layout**: single memory with fixed regions (header + cursors, ring, arena, guest heap).
- **Zero dynamic heap allocations during layout updates**; sub-millisecond execution goal.

## Deliverables

- `spec/OPCODE.md` — the new fixed-size opcode protocol spec (supersedes the variable-length format in `spec/BINARY_PROTOCOL.md`, which stays for history with a pointer).
- `lib/rust/` workspace with `pathland-opcode` (+ `pathland-layout` producing opcodes).
- Golden byte vectors for the new opcodes in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`.
- Update `AGENTS.md` / `README.md` to the new architecture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Opcode` is exactly 16 bytes, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, verified by `size_of` test.
- [ ] Ring buffer with cursor + frame-counter framing works SPSC (round-trip test).
- [ ] Arena allocates/reads var-length data; opcode refs decode correctly.
- [ ] `LAYOUT_SET_ORIGIN` / `LAYOUT_SET_SIZE` emit correct bounds for a minimal VStack/HStack/Text tree.
- [ ] Golden conformance vectors pass (`cargo test`).
- [ ] `pathland-opcode` / `pathland-layout` build `no_std` + `alloc` and target `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- [ ] Zero-alloc layout path proven with a counting allocator test.

## Dependencies

None. Blocks Goals 2, 3, 4, 5.

## Goal

Build the fixed-size **16-byte opcode engine** — the foundational protocol layer for the Pathland Rust core. All layout math, tree bounds, and drawing instructions are emitted by the WASM guest engine into a contiguous, fixed 16-byte opcode ring buffer in linear memory.

This is the foundation of the new Rust-first architecture (see `AGENTS.md`). Blocks Goals 2–5.

## Scope

New Rust workspace `lib/rust/`, crate `pathland-opcode` (and the `pathland-layout` layout engine hook that emits into it):

- **Opcode struct**: `#[repr(C, packed)]` — `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | Payload A (4B) | Payload B (4B) | Payload C (4B)` = exactly 16 bytes, little-endian, L1 cache-line aligned (64B line = 4 opcodes).
- **Categories / command tables**: TREE, LAYOUT, STYLE/DRAW, DRAW, EVENT, GESTURE, META. Includes `LAYOUT_SET_ORIGIN` (`nodeId, x, y`) + `LAYOUT_SET_SIZE` (`nodeId, w, h`) split-bounds opcodes.
- **Ring buffer**: contiguous power-of-two slot array; single-producer (guest engine) / single-consumer (host renderer), lock-free via `read`/`write` cursors + monotonic **frame counter** in a fixed header block. Host detects completed frames by watching the write cursor + frame counter.
- **Arena for variable-length data**: bump arena region in linear memory for strings, token paths, and child-id lists; opcodes reference it via `(offset, byteLength)` packed into A/B/C so every opcode stays 16 bytes.
- **Fixed linear-memory layout**: single memory with fixed regions (header + cursors, ring, arena, guest heap).
- **Zero dynamic heap allocations during layout updates**; sub-millisecond execution goal.

## Deliverables

- `spec/OPCODE.md` — the new fixed-size opcode protocol spec (supersedes the variable-length format in `spec/BINARY_PROTOCOL.md`, which stays for history with a pointer).
- `lib/rust/` workspace with `pathland-opcode` (+ `pathland-layout` producing opcodes).
- Golden byte vectors for the new opcodes in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`.
- Update `AGENTS.md` / `README.md` to the new architecture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Opcode` is exactly 16 bytes, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, verified by `size_of` test.
- [ ] Ring buffer with cursor + frame-counter framing works SPSC (round-trip test).
- [ ] Arena allocates/reads var-length data; opcode refs decode correctly.
- [ ] `LAYOUT_SET_ORIGIN` / `LAYOUT_SET_SIZE` emit correct bounds for a minimal VStack/HStack/Text tree.
- [ ] Golden conformance vectors pass (`cargo test`).
- [ ] `pathland-opcode` / `pathland-layout` build `no_std` + `alloc` and target `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- [ ] Zero-alloc layout path proven with a counting allocator test.

## Dependencies

None. Blocks Goals 2, 3, 4, 5.

289:     slots: &'a [u8],

313:     /// Consume all frames produced since the last call, advancing `readCursor`.
314:     ///
315:     /// Returns at most one `Frame` (all new opcodes since the last drain). If
316:     /// the producer produced multiple frames before this call they coalesce.
317:     pub fn frames(&mut self) -> Vec<Frame<'a>> {
318:         let frame_count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
319:         if self.consumed >= frame_count {
320:             return Vec::new();
321:         }
322:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
323:         let start = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, mask);
324:         let end = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
325: 
326:         // The POC producer flushes before the ring fills, so `end >= start`
327:         // always holds. Guard against a wrapped ring by draining nothing; a
328:         // wrapped producer must flush first (see OPCODE.md backpressure).
329:         if end < start {
330:             return Vec::new();
331:         }
332: 
333:         let frames = vec![Frame {
334:             slots: self.slots,
335:             arena: self.arena,
336:             start: start * Opcode::SIZE,
337:             end: end * Opcode::SIZE,
338:         }];
339: 
340:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, end as u32);
341:         self.consumed = frame_count;
342:         frames
343:     }

1: //! Linear-memory layout and the 64-byte header block.
2: //!
3: //! The guest engine and host share a single linear memory with fixed regions:
4: //! header block → ring buffer → arena. See `spec/OPCODE.md`.
5: 
6: use crate::opcode::OPCODE_SIZE;
7: 
8: /// Magic value written at header offset 0 (`"PLPL"`).
9: pub const MAGIC: u32 = 0x504C_504C;
10: /// Wire protocol version.
11: pub const PROTOCOL_VERSION: u16 = 1;
12: 
13: /// Default ring capacity in slots (power of two).
14: pub const DEFAULT_SLOT_COUNT: usize = 4096;
15: /// Default arena capacity in bytes.
16: pub const DEFAULT_ARENA_BYTES: usize = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB
17: 
18: // --- Header field offsets (64-byte header) ---
19: /// Byte offset of `magic: u32`.
20: pub const OFF_MAGIC: usize = 0x00;
21: /// Byte offset of `version: u16`.
22: pub const OFF_VERSION: usize = 0x04;
23: /// Byte offset of `ringOffset: u32`.
24: pub const OFF_RING_OFFSET: usize = 0x06;
25: /// Byte offset of `ringBytes: u32`.
26: pub const OFF_RING_BYTES: usize = 0x0A;
27: /// Byte offset of `slotCount: u32`.
28: pub const OFF_SLOT_COUNT: usize = 0x0E;
29: /// Byte offset of `arenaOffset: u32`.
30: pub const OFF_ARENA_OFFSET: usize = 0x12;
31: /// Byte offset of `arenaBytes: u32`.
32: pub const OFF_ARENA_BYTES: usize = 0x14;
33: /// Byte offset of `arenaCursor: u32` (guest-owned).
34: pub const OFF_ARENA_CURSOR: usize = 0x18;
35: /// Byte offset of `readCursor: u32` (host-owned).
36: pub const OFF_READ_CURSOR: usize = 0x1C;
37: /// Byte offset of `writeCursor: u32` (guest-owned).
38: pub const OFF_WRITE_CURSOR: usize = 0x20;
39: /// Byte offset of `frameCount: u32` (guest-owned).
40: pub const OFF_FRAME_COUNT: usize = 0x24;
41: /// Total header size in bytes.
42: pub const HEADER_SIZE: usize = 0x40;
43: 
44: /// The fixed layout of the shared linear memory.
45: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
46: pub struct MemoryLayout {
47:     /// Ring capacity in slots (must be a power of two).
48:     pub slot_count: usize,
49:     /// Arena capacity in bytes.
50:     pub arena_bytes: usize,
51: }
52: 
53: impl Default for MemoryLayout {
54:     fn default() -> Self {
55:         Self {
56:             slot_count: DEFAULT_SLOT_COUNT,
57:             arena_bytes: DEFAULT_ARENA_BYTES,
58:         }
59:     }
60: }
61: 
62: impl MemoryLayout {
63:     /// Ring region byte length.
64:     #[inline]
65:     pub fn ring_bytes(&self) -> usize {
66:         self.slot_count * OPCODE_SIZE
67:     }
68: 
69:     /// Total linear memory size: header + ring + arena.
70:     pub fn total_bytes(&self) -> usize {
71:         HEADER_SIZE + self.ring_bytes() + self.arena_bytes
72:     }
73: 
74:     /// Byte offset of the ring region (directly after the header).
75:     #[inline]
76:     pub fn ring_offset(&self) -> usize {
77:         HEADER_SIZE
78:     }
79: 
80:     /// Byte offset of the arena region (directly after the ring).
81:     #[inline]
82:     pub fn arena_offset(&self) -> usize {
83:         self.ring_offset() + self.ring_bytes()
84:     }
85: 
86:     /// Ring mask for wrapping a cursor (slot count is a power of two).
87:     #[inline]
88:     pub fn ring_mask(&self) -> usize {
89:         debug_assert!(self.slot_count.is_power_of_two());
90:         self.slot_count - 1
91:     }
92: }
93: 
94: /// Low-level accessors for the header block.
95: ///
96: /// All accesses use explicit little-endian byte reads so the header can sit at
97: /// an arbitrary alignment within the linear memory.
98: pub(crate) mod header {
99:     use super::*;
100: 
101:     #[inline]
102:     pub(crate) fn get_u32(buf: &[u8], off: usize) -> u32 {
103:         u32::from_le_bytes(buf[off..off + 4].try_into().unwrap())
104:     }
105: 
106:     #[inline]
107:     pub(crate) fn set_u32(buf: &mut [u8], off: usize, value: u32) {
108:         buf[off..off + 4].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
109:     }
110: 
111:     #[inline]
112:     pub(crate) fn get_u16(buf: &[u8], off: usize) -> u16 {
113:         u16::from_le_bytes(buf[off..off + 2].try_into().unwrap())
114:     }
115: 
116:     /// Initialize a zeroed header for the given layout.
117:     pub(crate) fn init(buf: &mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) {
118:         buf[..HEADER_SIZE].fill(0);
119:         set_u32(buf, OFF_MAGIC, MAGIC);
120:         buf[OFF_VERSION..OFF_VERSION + 2].copy_from_slice(&PROTOCOL_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
121:         set_u32(buf, OFF_RING_OFFSET, layout.ring_offset() as u32);
122:         set_u32(buf, OFF_RING_BYTES, layout.ring_bytes() as u32);
123:         set_u32(buf, OFF_SLOT_COUNT, layout.slot_count as u32);
124:         set_u32(buf, OFF_ARENA_OFFSET, layout.arena_offset() as u32);
125:         set_u32(buf, OFF_ARENA_BYTES, layout.arena_bytes as u32);
126:         set_u32(buf, OFF_ARENA_CURSOR, 0);
127:         set_u32(buf, OFF_READ_CURSOR, 0);
128:         set_u32(buf, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, 0);
129:         set_u32(buf, OFF_FRAME_COUNT, 0);
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Validate a header against a layout; returns false if the memory is not a
133:     /// valid Pathland linear memory.
134:     #[allow(dead_code)]
135:     pub(crate) fn validate(buf: &[u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> bool {
136:         if buf.len() < HEADER_SIZE {
137:             return false;
138:         }
139:         let magic = get_u32(buf, OFF_MAGIC);
140:         if magic != MAGIC {
141:             return false;
142:         }
143:         let version = get_u16(buf, OFF_VERSION);
144:         if version != PROTOCOL_VERSION {
145:             return false;
146:         }
147:         get_u32(buf, OFF_SLOT_COUNT) as usize == layout.slot_count
148:             && get_u32(buf, OFF_ARENA_BYTES) as usize == layout.arena_bytes
149:     }
150: }

153: mod tests {

155:     use super::*;

201: The guest engine and host share a **single linear memory**. Regions are fixed at module start:
202: 
203: ```
204: +───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
205: | 0x0000  Header block (64 B)  — cursors, frame counter, layout  |
206: | 0x0040  Ring buffer (16 B × slotCount)                         |
207: | ...      (slots densely packed, 64-byte aligned base)          |
208: | 0x10040 Arena (bump region for strings / token paths / lists)  |
209: | ...                                                            |
210: +───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
211: ```
212: 
213: ### Header block (64 bytes)
214: 
215: | Offset | Size | Field | Producer | Description |
216: |--------|------|-------|----------|-------------|
217: | 0x00 | 4 | `magic` | — | `0x504C504C` (`PLPL`) |
218: | 0x04 | 2 | `version` | — | Wire protocol version (1) |
219: | 0x06 | 4 | `ringOffset` | — | Byte offset of the ring region |
220: | 0x0A | 4 | `ringBytes` | — | Byte length of the ring region |
221: | 0x0E | 4 | `slotCount` | — | Number of ring slots (power of two) |
222: | 0x12 | 4 | `arenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the arena region |
223: | 0x14 | 4 | `arenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the arena region |
224: | 0x18 | 4 | `arenaCursor` | guest | Next free byte in the arena |
225: | 0x1C | 4 | `readCursor` | host | Ring slot the host has consumed up to |
226: | 0x20 | 4 | `writeCursor` | guest | Ring slot the guest has written up to |
227: | 0x24 | 4 | `frameCount` | guest | Monotonic completed-frame counter |
228: | 0x28 | 36 | reserved | — | Zero |
229: 
230: ### Ring buffer
231: 
232: - Contiguous array of **16-byte slots**; `slotCount` is a **power of two** (wrap via mask, no modulo).
233: - **Producer** (guest) writes at `writeCursor`, then advances `writeCursor` and increments `frameCount` at frame end.
234: - **Consumer** (host) reads from `readCursor` up to `writeCursor`; after draining a frame it advances `readCursor`.
235: - **Backpressure**: the producer must not advance `writeCursor` past `readCursor` (ring full). The producer SHOULD flush a frame before the ring is full.
236: - **Frame boundary detection**: the host watches `frameCount`. When it advances, exactly one frame (all slots from the previously consumed `readCursor` to the current `writeCursor`) is complete.
237: 
238: ### Arena
239: 
240: - A pre-allocated **bump region** for variable-length data (strings, token paths).
241: - Every arena entry is **self-describing**: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`.
242: - Opcodes reference entries by their **byte offset** (`arenaRef`), so an entry's length is read directly from the arena — all opcodes stay 16 bytes.
243: - The guest advances `arenaCursor` monotonically (no free-list, no fragmentation). The arena MAY be reset via `META::RESET`.
244: 
245: ---
246: 
247: ## Colors
248: 
249: Literal colors are **sRGB** (IEC 61966-2-1, D65 white point), packed as `0xAARRGGBB`:
250: 
251: - `AA`: alpha (0x00 transparent – 0xFF opaque)
252: - `RR`: red, `GG`: green, `BB`: blue
253: 
254: Stored little-endian in a `u32` payload. Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation remain **renderer-owned** (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)).
255: 
256: ---
257: 
258: ## Design Token System
259: 
260: ### Core Principle
261: 
262: > **The renderer owns the defaults. The application owns the overrides.**
263: 
264: This ensures a native look-and-feel by default and cross-platform consistency when the application overrides tokens.
265: 
266: ### Responsibilities
267: 
268: | Aspect | Owner | Responsibility |
269: |--------|-------|----------------|
270: | **Default Token Values** | Renderer | Define platform-appropriate defaults for all standard tokens |
271: | **Token Overrides** | Application | Specify overrides for cross-platform consistency |
272: | **Token Resolution** | Renderer | Resolve final token values (override or default) |
273: | **Platform Adaptation** | Renderer | Adapt default token values to platform conventions |
274: 
275: ### Token Identification
276: 
277: Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`, `font.body`), case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. The `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) references a token path stored in the arena; `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides a token's value globally.
278: 
279: ### Token Resolution Algorithm
280: 
281: ```
282: FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath: string) -> PropertyValue:
283:     IF applicationOverrides.has(tokenPath):
284:         RETURN applicationOverrides[tokenPath]
285:     ELSE IF rendererDefaults.has(tokenPath):
286:         RETURN rendererDefaults[tokenPath]
287:     ELSE IF hasParentToken(tokenPath):
288:         RETURN resolveToken(getParentPath(tokenPath))
289:     ELSE:
290:         RETURN getFallbackValue(tokenPath)
291: ```
292: 
293: ### Renderer Responsibilities
294: 
295: The renderer MUST:
296: 
297: 1. Provide platform-appropriate defaults for all standard tokens (e.g. `color.primary`, `font.body.size`, `space.md`).
298: 2. Accept `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides.
299: 3. Resolve design-token references in properties.
300: 4. Fall back to defaults when no override exists.
301: 5. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.
302: 
303: The application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` and reference tokens via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; it MUST NOT assume specific default token values.
304: 
305: ### Standard Token Catalog
306: 
307: Required core tokens (renderer MUST support with platform-appropriate defaults): `color.primary`, `color.secondary`, `color.background`, `color.surface`, `color.text.primary`, `color.text.secondary`, `color.border`, `font.body.size`, `font.body.weight`, `font.body.family`, `space.xs`–`space.lg`.
308: 
309: Recommended extended tokens: `color.success`, `color.warning`, `color.danger`, `color.info`, `font.heading.1`–`font.heading.6`, `font.size.heading.1`–`6`, `radius.sm`/`md`, `elevation.low`/`high`, `opacity.disabled`.
310: 
311: ---
312: 
313: ## Frame Lifecycle
314: 
315: A frame is a batch of delta opcodes produced by one `emit` pass:
316: 
317: 1. Guest begins a frame.
318: 2. Guest emits the delta opcodes (tree structure and/or property changes) into consecutive ring slots.
319: 3. Guest allocates strings in the arena as needed.
320: 4. Guest `end_frame()`: publishes `writeCursor`, then increments `frameCount`.
321: 5. Host observes `frameCount` change, drains `[readCursor, writeCursor)`, advances `readCursor`.
322: 
323: Because the ring and arena are plain memory, the guest publishes via a single release store of `frameCount`; the host acquires on read.
324: 
325: ---
326: 
327: ## Conformance
328: 
329: Golden byte vectors for this protocol are in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md).

## Linear Memory Layout

The guest engine and host share a **single linear memory**. Regions are fixed at module start:

```
+───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
| 0x0000  Header block (64 B)  — cursors, frame counter, layout  |
| 0x0040  Ring buffer (16 B × slotCount)                         |
| ...      (slots densely packed, 64-byte aligned base)          |
| 0x10040 Arena (bump region for strings / token paths / lists)  |
| ...                                                            |
+───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
```

### Header block (64 bytes)

| Offset | Size | Field | Producer | Description |
|--------|------|-------|----------|-------------|
| 0x00 | 4 | `magic` | — | `0x504C504C` (`PLPL`) |
| 0x04 | 2 | `version` | — | Wire protocol version (1) |
| 0x06 | 4 | `ringOffset` | — | Byte offset of the ring region |
| 0x0A | 4 | `ringBytes` | — | Byte length of the ring region |
| 0x0E | 4 | `slotCount` | — | Number of ring slots (power of two) |
| 0x12 | 4 | `arenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the arena region |
| 0x14 | 4 | `arenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the arena region |
| 0x18 | 4 | `arenaCursor` | guest | Next free byte in the arena |
| 0x1C | 4 | `readCursor` | host | Ring slot the host has consumed up to |
| 0x20 | 4 | `writeCursor` | guest | Ring slot the guest has written up to |
| 0x24 | 4 | `frameCount` | guest | Monotonic completed-frame counter |
| 0x28 | 36 | reserved | — | Zero |

### Ring buffer

- Contiguous array of **16-byte slots**; `slotCount` is a **power of two** (wrap via mask, no modulo).
- **Producer** (guest) writes at `writeCursor`, then advances `writeCursor` and increments `frameCount` at frame end.
- **Consumer** (host) reads from `readCursor` up to `writeCursor`; after draining a frame it advances `readCursor`.
- **Backpressure**: the producer must not advance `writeCursor` past `readCursor` (ring full). The producer SHOULD flush a frame before the ring is full.
- **Frame boundary detection**: the host watches `frameCount`. When it advances, exactly one frame (all slots from the previously consumed `readCursor` to the current `writeCursor`) is complete.

### Arena

- A pre-allocated **bump region** for variable-length data (strings, token paths).
- Every arena entry is **self-describing**: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`.
- Opcodes reference entries by their **byte offset** (`arenaRef`), so an entry's length is read directly from the arena — all opcodes stay 16 bytes.
- The guest advances `arenaCursor` monotonically (no free-list, no fragmentation). The arena MAY be reset via `META::RESET`.

---

## Colors

Literal colors are **sRGB** (IEC 61966-2-1, D65 white point), packed as `0xAARRGGBB`:

- `AA`: alpha (0x00 transparent – 0xFF opaque)
- `RR`: red, `GG`: green, `BB`: blue

Stored little-endian in a `u32` payload. Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation remain **renderer-owned** (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)).

---

## Design Token System

### Core Principle

> **The renderer owns the defaults. The application owns the overrides.**

This ensures a native look-and-feel by default and cross-platform consistency when the application overrides tokens.

### Responsibilities

| Aspect | Owner | Responsibility |
|--------|-------|----------------|
| **Default Token Values** | Renderer | Define platform-appropriate defaults for all standard tokens |
| **Token Overrides** | Application | Specify overrides for cross-platform consistency |
| **Token Resolution** | Renderer | Resolve final token values (override or default) |
| **Platform Adaptation** | Renderer | Adapt default token values to platform conventions |

### Token Identification

Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`, `font.body`), case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. The `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) references a token path stored in the arena; `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides a token's value globally.

### Token Resolution Algorithm

```
FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath: string) -> PropertyValue:
    IF applicationOverrides.has(tokenPath):
        RETURN applicationOverrides[tokenPath]
    ELSE IF rendererDefaults.has(tokenPath):
        RETURN rendererDefaults[tokenPath]
    ELSE IF hasParentToken(tokenPath):
        RETURN resolveToken(getParentPath(tokenPath))
    ELSE:
        RETURN getFallbackValue(tokenPath)
```

### Renderer Responsibilities

The renderer MUST:

1. Provide platform-appropriate defaults for all standard tokens (e.g. `color.primary`, `font.body.size`, `space.md`).
2. Accept `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides.
3. Resolve design-token references in properties.
4. Fall back to defaults when no override exists.
5. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.

The application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` and reference tokens via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; it MUST NOT assume specific default token values.

### Standard Token Catalog

Required core tokens (renderer MUST support with platform-appropriate defaults): `color.primary`, `color.secondary`, `color.background`, `color.surface`, `color.text.primary`, `color.text.secondary`, `color.border`, `font.body.size`, `font.body.weight`, `font.body.family`, `space.xs`–`space.lg`.

Recommended extended tokens: `color.success`, `color.warning`, `color.danger`, `color.info`, `font.heading.1`–`font.heading.6`, `font.size.heading.1`–`6`, `radius.sm`/`md`, `elevation.low`/`high`, `opacity.disabled`.

---

## Frame Lifecycle

A frame is a batch of delta opcodes produced by one `emit` pass:

1. Guest begins a frame.
2. Guest emits the delta opcodes (tree structure and/or property changes) into consecutive ring slots.
3. Guest allocates strings in the arena as needed.
4. Guest `end_frame()`: publishes `writeCursor`, then increments `frameCount`.
5. Host observes `frameCount` change, drains `[readCursor, writeCursor)`, advances `readCursor`.

Because the ring and arena are plain memory, the guest publishes via a single release store of `frameCount`; the host acquires on read.

---

## Conformance

Golden byte vectors for this protocol are in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md).

Actually, the user is asking me to explain the distinction. Let me reason from the spec and the design.

From OPCODE.md:
- EVENT (0x03) — host → guest — "Discrete events" — Tap, hover, key, etc.
- GESTURE (0x04) — host → guest — "Gesture updates" — Began/changed/ended/cancelled

The distinction: A TAP is a discrete, one-shot event (fire-and-forget). A GESTURE is a continuous, multi-phase interaction lifecycle (began → changed → ... → ended/cancelled), like a drag, scroll, pinch, or swipe. parts.text:
Now I have a clear picture from the historical implementation. Let me answer the user's conceptual question about EVENT:TAP vs GESTURE:UPDATE.

The distinction:
- EVENT:TAP is a discrete, fire-and-forget event (host → guest): a tap happened, at coordinates. It has no lifecycle, no continuity. It's the "onTap" handler.
- GESTURE:UPDATE is a lifecycle-aware gesture update (host → guest): began → changed → ended → cancelled, with a gestureType + gestureId to track an in-progress gesture across multiple updates. It's for continuous interactions: drag, long-press, pinch, rotate, swipe. A gesture is stateful over time; the guest correlates updates by gestureId.

In the historical protocol, there was even overlap: TAP existed both as EventType.TAP (0x01, discrete) and GestureType.TAP (0x10, lifecycle version). And in the SwiftUI world: `onTapGesture` sugar = discrete tap event; `TapGesture().onEnded {}` = lifecycle gesture.

The current OPCODE.md spec keeps this: EVENT = discrete (tap/hover/key), GESTURE = lifecycle updates (began/changed/ended/cancelled) with gestureType+state+gestureId.

The user's questions:
1. "What is gesture:update?" — The single GESTURE command that carries a gesture lifecycle update: A=targetId, B=(state<<8)|gestureType, C=gestureId. It's the only gesture command currently defined. It's how the host tells the guest that a gesture recognized on a node progressed.
2. "Event:tap is not a gesture?" — Correct: TAP is a discrete event, not a gesture. Discrete tap = one-shot fire-and-forget (click/tap, coordinates, no lifecycle). Gesture TAP (in the legacy) was a lifecycle version with began/ended. In the current spec, GESTURE only has UPDATE; a "tap gesture" via GESTURE would just be began+ended state updates.

Let me explain concisely with references. This is an informational question in plan mode. No edits.

Good question — this distinction comes straight from the legacy design (still reflected in the current spec). The key is **discrete vs. lifecycle**:

**EVENT (0x03) — discrete, fire-and-forget.** One-shot signals with no continuity: `TAP` at (x,y), `HOVER`, `KEY`. The guest gets it once and reacts. This is your `onTap` / `onClick` handler.

**GESTURE (0x04) — lifecycle, stateful over time.** `GESTURE::UPDATE` (`A=targetId, B=(state<<8)|gestureType, C=gestureId`) tells the guest that a *recognized, in-progress* gesture progressed: `BEGAN → CHANGED → ENDED/CANCELLED` (`gesture.rs` states, legacy `constants.ts:193-198`). The `gestureId` correlates a continuous stream of updates for the *same* interaction — a drag that starts, moves 40 times, then ends is one gesture, many `UPDATE`s. Continuous types: DRAG, LONG_PRESS, SWIPE, PINCH, ROTATE (`constants.ts:183-190`).

**So: EVENT:TAP is not a gesture** — it's the discrete "a tap happened" signal. The current spec has **no** GESTURE:TAP command; tap only exists as an EVENT. (The legacy protocol had both: `EventType.TAP` discrete vs `GestureType.TAP` lifecycle via `TapGesture().onEnded{}` — mirroring SwiftUI's `onTapGesture` vs `TapGesture().onEnded{}`.)

Why both? A discrete tap is cheap and stateless — the renderer just reports "tapped here." A gesture implies *recognition* (the renderer owns the recognizer, per stateless-renderer principles: it watches pointer movement and only reports once it recognizes a drag/long-press). That's a protocol-level distinction worth keeping — my conformance plan locks both correctly.

One nuance for the vectors: `gestureType`/`state` byte packing isn't fully specified in OPCODE.md:172 (values live only in legacy history). I'll document the values (BEGAN=0x00…CANCELLED=0x03, and type IDs) in the vector before locking bytes.

events and gestures are not the same thing in Pathland, though they are closely related. Think of events as the raw inputs and gestures as the high-level interpretations of those inputs.
Here is the breakdown of the differences:

1. Events (The Raw Input)
What they are: Events are low-level system notifications that something has happened, such as a user touching the screen, pressing a key on a keyboard, or moving a mouse pointer.
Examples: Touch down, touch moved, touch up, or keyboard presses.

2. Gestures (The Interpreted Actions)
What they are: Gestures are high-level abstractions built on top of raw touch events. A gesture takes a sequence of raw touch events, analyzes them, and determines if they match a specific pattern (like a tap, a long press, or a drag).

 # Pathland Project - AI Agent Guide
 
 This document provides essential context for AI agents (or human contributors) working on the **Pathland** protocol. It captures the project's direction, architectural decisions, and implementation details to ensure consistency.
 
 **Last Updated**: August 14, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## New Direction: Rust WASM Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine compiled to WASM** ("WASM guest engine")
 > that emits the application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack,
 > Text, spacing, padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer**
 > into shared linear memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and
 > modifiers are written in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API; other languages consume
 > the components as **WASM/WIT** components.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors).
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`STYLE` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### Rust Workspace (`lib/rust/`)
 
 ```
 crates/pathland-opcode/   # 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, memory layout (no_std)
 crates/pathland-engine/   # retained view tree -> declarative TREE/STYLE opcodes,
                           #   diff-based reactive emission (zero-alloc steady state)
 crates/pathland-host/     # host reader: ring -> native-element description (std layer)
 wit/pathland.wit          # WIT component-world definitions (Goal 3+)
 ```
 
 - Test: `cd lib/rust && cargo test` (runs all crates).
 - WASM build: `RUSTC=~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
   (the Homebrew `cargo` on PATH uses a rustc without the wasm std; use the rustup toolchain's rustc).
 
 ### POC Goals (issues #12–#16)
 
 | # | Goal | Status |
 |---|------|--------|
 | 12 | 16-byte opcode engine | **In progress** (`feature/opcode-engine` branch) |
 | 13 | Core components & modifiers in Rust | Planned |
 | 14 | TypeScript browser demo via WASM/WIT | Planned |
 | 15 | Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo | Planned |
 | 16 | Rust desktop app with GTK4 renderer | Planned |
 
 ---
 
 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust WASM opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the New Direction section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
-- **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND events/gestures (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic
+- **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic
 
 ---
 
 ## Protocol Quick Reference
 
 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | STYLE | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
-| EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Tap, hover, key, etc. |
-| GESTURE | 0x04 | Host → Guest | Began/changed/ended/cancelled |
-| META | 0x05 | Both | Reset, environment |
+| EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
+| META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment |
 
 ### Component Types (u16)
 
 | Component | ID |
 |-----------|----|
 | HSTACK | 0x0001 |
 | VSTACK | 0x0002 |
 | TEXT | 0x0003 |
 | BUTTON | 0x0004 |
 | IMAGE | 0x0005 |
 | SWITCH | 0x0006 |
 | TEXT_FIELD | 0x0007 |
 | SPACER | 0x0008 |
 | SCROLLVIEW | 0x0009 |
 | LIST | 0x000A |
 | GRID | 0x000B |
 | COMMENT | 0x000C |
 
 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, JUSTIFICATION=0x0003, PADDING=0x0004, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005  
 **Text**: TEXT=0x000A, TEXT_ALIGNMENT=0x000C, LINE_LIMIT=0x000B, TRUNCATION_MODE=0x000D  
 **Style**: COLOR=0x100A, FONT_SIZE=0x1007, FONT_WEIGHT=0x1008, FONT_FAMILY=0x1009, BACKGROUND_COLOR=0x1001, BORDER_WIDTH=0x1003, BORDER_COLOR=0x1004, BORDER_RADIUS=0x1005, OPACITY=0x100D, VISIBLE=0x100E, Z_INDEX=0x100F, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=0x1010, PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT=0x1012-0x1015  
 **Special**: WIDTH=0x100B (use -1=FILL, -2=HUG_CONTENT), HEIGHT=0x100C  
 **Semantic**: ROLE=0x2001, STATE=0x2002, ENABLED=0x2003, SELECTED=0x2004
 
 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent and overrides. Renderer defines visual appearance and behavior.
 
 - Renderer owns design tokens, default values, semantic-token resolution, interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme logic
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 
 Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system).
 
 ---
 
 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-opcode/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-engine` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-engine`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-opcode` encoding/emitters
 3. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-engine`/`pathland-host` + tests
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-opcode`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ---
 
 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |
 |--------------|-----------|---------|
 | Renderer stores application state | Violates statelessness | Application owns the tree |
 | Engine computes layout / emits rects | Violates declarative model | Emit structure + constraints; native elements lay out |
 | Send full trees | Inefficient | Diff-based reactive emission |
 | String property names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | String component names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
 | Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
 | Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |
 
 ---
 
 ## Project Status

 ---
 
 ## Quick Start
 
 1. Read this file and `spec/OPCODE.md`
 2. Run tests: `cd lib/rust && cargo test` (runs all crates)
 3. Build for wasm32: `RUSTC=~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
 4. Make small changes, verify they work
 
 ---
 
 ## Pathland Mindset
 
 **Always remember**:
 1. Protocol is King
 2. Renderers are Dumb (execute commands only)
 3. Applications are Smart (generate commands)
 4. Only Changes Matter (transmit mutations / reactive emission)
 5. Binary is Beautiful (efficient, deterministic)
 
 **When in doubt**: Check `spec/OPCODE.md`, the conformance vectors in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, and the reference implementation (`pathland-opcode`). Ask: "Does this maintain stateless renderers?"  # Pathland Protocol
 
 > A cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol inspired by SwiftUI
 
 ## Overview
 
 Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
 multiple renderer backends. It's inspired by SwiftUI's declarative syntax, but
 designed to be **language-agnostic** and **platform-agnostic**.
 
 As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust engine compiled to WASM** ("WASM guest
 engine"). It emits the application's **declarative view structure** — VStack,
 HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring
 buffer** into shared linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode
 stream onto that platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements,
 HTML) and those native elements lay themselves out.
 
 **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
 *what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
 signals in the application ensure only changed nodes emit opcodes, so an
 unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
 
 ## Core Principles
 
-- **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and gestures
+- **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and raw inputs
 - **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode
 - **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine emits structure + constraint properties (spacing, padding, alignment); native renderers compute positions
 - **Native elements everywhere**: GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent
 - **Reactive emission**: only the nodes that changed emit opcodes; steady state emits zero
 - **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
 - **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
 - **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
 - **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes
 - **Worker-first heritage**: the architecture keeps the application logic separable from rendering, and WASM/WIT makes components consumable from any language
 
 ## Documentation
 
 ### Specification
 
 - [Opcode Protocol](./spec/OPCODE.md) — **Primary specification** — fixed 16-byte opcodes, ring buffer, arena, reactive emission, design tokens
 - [Conformance Test Vectors](./spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte arrays for validating implementations
 
 ## Rust Workspace
 
 The implementation is under [`lib/rust/`](./lib/rust/):
 
 | Crate | Responsibility |
 |-------|----------------|
 | `pathland-opcode` | 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, bump arena, linear-memory layout (`no_std`) |
 | `pathland-engine` | Retained view tree → declarative `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes; diff-based reactive emission (zero-alloc steady state) |
 | `pathland-host` | Host reader: ring → native-element description (`std` convenience layer) |

 ```
 
 ### Build for wasm32
 
 ```bash
 RUSTC=~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc \
   cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
 ```

 Component and property IDs are defined in `pathland-opcode`'s
 [`constants.rs`](./lib/rust/crates/pathland-opcode/src/constants.rs) and
 documented in [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md). Component types include `HSTACK`,

 (`SPACING`, `PADDING`, `ALIGNMENT`, …) drive native layout, and `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`
 use `-1` = FILL, `-2` = HUG_CONTENT.

 The renderer owns default token values; the application owns overrides.
 Tokens are identified by dot-separated paths (`color.primary`, `space.2`) and
 referenced via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type or overridden globally with

 This document provides **golden byte arrays** for the Pathland opcode protocol (see [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)). A conforming implementation MUST:
 
 - encode each opcode to exactly these 16 bytes, and

 # Pathland Opcode Protocol Specification
 
 **Wire protocol version:** 1
 **Status:** Draft
 **Format:** Fixed-size (16-byte) opcode engine
 **Last Updated:** August 13, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Overview
 
 The Pathland Opcode Protocol is the **fixed-size instruction engine** at the heart of the Rust-first architecture. The **WASM guest engine** emits the application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment — as a stream of fixed 16-byte opcodes into a **ring buffer** in **linear memory**. The host renderer consumes the ring and maps the structure onto that platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML).
 
 **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** Native renderers lay out their own native elements from the constraint properties the engine passes through. This is the Pathland principle: *always render through that platform's native elements.*
 
 This specification supersedes the historical variable-length binary instruction format (which has been removed from the repository).
 
 ### Goals
 
 - **Sub-millisecond execution**: every opcode is a fixed 16 bytes; emission is a diff over the retained tree with **zero dynamic heap allocations** in the steady state.
 - **L1 CPU cache alignment**: a 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes**. Ring slots are 16-byte aligned and densely packed.
 - **Reactive emission**: only the nodes that changed emit opcodes. An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes (see [Reactive Emission](#reactive-emission)).
 - **Linear, deterministic decoding**: the host walks the ring with a single cursor.
 
 ### Core Principles
 
 1. **Fixed-size instructions**: every opcode is exactly 16 bytes — no length prefixes, no skippable-variable framing.
 2. **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine describes *what* the UI is (stacks, text, constraints), never *where* it is. Native elements compute their own positions.
 3. **Numeric IDs**: categories, commands, component types, and properties are numeric.
 4. **Native elements**: renderers map the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 5. **Zero-copy**: the ring and arena are plain regions of the same linear memory shared with the host.
 6. **Single-producer / single-consumer**: the guest engine produces; the host renderer consumes. No locks required.
 
 ---
 
 ## Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 | Field | Size | Offset | Description |
 |-------|------|--------|-------------|
 | `Category` | 1B | 0 | Opcode category (see [Category Table](#category-table)) |
 | `Command` | 1B | 1 | Command within the category (see [Command Tables](#command-tables)) |
 | `Flags` | 2B | 2 | Category/command-specific flags |
 | `A` | 4B | 4 | Primary payload |
 | `B` | 4B | 8 | Secondary payload |
 | `C` | 4B | 12 | Tertiary payload |
 
 All multi-byte values are **little-endian**. The Rust reference type is `#[repr(C, packed)]`:
 
 ```rust
 #[repr(C, packed)]
 pub struct Opcode {
     pub category: u8,
     pub command: u8,
     pub flags: u16,
     pub a: u32,
     pub b: u32,
     pub c: u32,
 }
 ```
 
 `size_of::<Opcode>() == 16`.
 
 ### Payload encoding conventions
 
 - **Float payloads** (`spacing`, `padding`, sizes) are stored as raw `f32` (IEEE 754) bit patterns in a `u32` field.
 - **Node IDs** are `u32`.
 - **Component types / property IDs** are `u16`; when packed into a 4-byte payload they occupy the low two bytes (the high bytes are reserved / zero unless documented).
 - **Arena references** are a `u32` byte offset into the arena region (see [Arena](#arena)).
 - **Colors** are packed `0xAARRGGBB` in sRGB (see [Colors](#colors)).
 
 ### Reserved ranges
 
 - `Category == 0` is reserved (invalid).
 - `Command == 0` in any category is reserved (invalid).
 - `Category 0x80-0xFF`: custom/extended categories.
 
 ---
 
 ## Category Table
 
 | Category | Value | Name | Producer | Description |
 |----------|-------|------|----------|-------------|
 | `TREE` | `0x01` | Tree mutations | Guest engine | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | `STYLE` | `0x02` | Constraints & tokens | Guest engine | Property values (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
-| `EVENT` | `0x03` | Discrete events | Host renderer | Tap, hover, key, etc. |
-| `GESTURE` | `0x04` | Gesture updates | Host renderer | Began/changed/ended/cancelled |
-| `META` | `0x05` | Control | Both | Reset, environment |
+| `EVENT` | `0x03` | Raw inputs | Host renderer | Pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
+| `META` | `0x04` | Control | Both | Reset, environment |
 
 ---
 
 ## Command Tables
 
 ### TREE (0x01)
 
 | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
 |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
 | `CREATE_NODE` | `0x01` | nodeId | componentType (u16, low) | 0 | — | Create a node of `componentType` |
 | `DELETE_NODE` | `0x02` | nodeId | 0 | 0 | — | Delete a node and its subtree |
 | `INSERT_CHILD` | `0x03` | parentId | childId | index | `0x0001` = append | Insert `childId` into `parentId` at `index` |
 | `REMOVE_CHILD` | `0x04` | parentId | childId | 0 | — | Remove `childId` from `parentId` |
 | `MOVE_CHILD` | `0x05` | parentId | childId | newIndex | `0x0001` = append | Move child to `newIndex` (after removal) |
 
 ### STYLE (0x02)
 
 The engine does not emit positions. `STYLE` carries the **constraint properties**
 that native renderers feed to their own layout — spacing, padding, alignment,
 FILL/HUG size hints, colors, fonts.
 
 | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
 |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
 | `SET_PROPERTY` | `0x01` | nodeId | propertyId (u16, low) + valueType (u8, high byte) | value | — | Set a constraint/style property; `value` depends on `valueType` |
 | `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x02` | arenaRef (path) | valueType (u8) | value | — | Override a design token; path is an arena string |
 | `SET_TEXT` | `0x03` | nodeId | arenaRef (utf8) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content |
 
 `SET_PROPERTY` encodes the value type in the **high byte of `B`** (bits 24–31) and the property id in the low two bytes:
 
 ```
 B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
 ```
 
 #### Value types
 
 | Value Type | Value | C / value encoding |
 |------------|-------|--------------------|
 | `U8` | `0x01` | low byte of C |
 | `U32` | `0x02` | u32 |
 | `I32` | `0x03` | i32 |
 | `F32` | `0x04` | f32 |
 | `STRING` | `0x05` | arenaRef (utf8) |
 | `ENUM` | `0x06` | low byte of C |
 | `COLOR` | `0x07` | packed `0xAARRGGBB` |
 | `DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x08` | arenaRef (token path) |
 
 #### Constraint properties for native layout
 
 The following properties drive native layout; the renderer maps them to its
 native equivalents (e.g. `SPACING` → GTK box spacing / CSS `gap`, `PADDING` →
 widget margin / CSS `padding`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` → size requests). Special
 `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1` = FILL (expand to available), `-2` = HUG_CONTENT
 (native intrinsic size).
 
 | Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
 |----------|-------|------|----------------|
 | `SPACING` | `0x0001` | F32 | Gap between children |
 | `ALIGNMENT` | `0x0002` | ENUM | Cross-axis alignment |
 | `JUSTIFICATION` | `0x0003` | ENUM | Main-axis distribution |
 | `PADDING` | `0x0004` | F32 | Uniform inner padding |
 | `WIDTH` | `0x100B` | F32 | Width hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
 | `HEIGHT` | `0x100C` | F32 | Height hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
 
 Full property catalog: see the Rust `constants.rs` (carried forward from the
 historical protocol).
 
 ### EVENT (0x03) — host → guest
 
-| Command | Value | A | B | C | Description |
-|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------------|
-| `TAP` | `0x01` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | Tap at viewport-relative point |
-| `HOVER` | `0x02` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | Pointer moved; Flags bit 0 = isHovering |
-| `KEY` | `0x03` | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | Key event; Flags bit 0 = down, bit 1 = repeat |
+Events are the **raw inputs**: the renderer reports what happened (a pointer
+went down/moved/up, a key went down/up) and resolves which node it hit via its
+own rendered-output tree. High-level interpretations — tap, drag, long-press —
+are built by the guest/app from these raw inputs and are **not** part of the
+protocol.
 
-### GESTURE (0x04) — host → guest
-
 | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
 |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
-| `UPDATE` | `0x01` | targetId | gestureType (u8) + state (u8, high byte) | gestureId | — | Gesture lifecycle update |
+| `POINTER_DOWN` | `0x01` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` | Pointer button pressed at viewport-relative point |
+| `POINTER_MOVE` | `0x02` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` / `HOVER_LEAVE` | Pointer moved (bit 0 = entered/hovering, bit 1 = leaving) |
+| `POINTER_UP` | `0x03` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` | Pointer button released at viewport-relative point |
+| `KEY_DOWN` | `0x04` | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` | Key pressed (bit 1 = auto-repeat) |
+| `KEY_UP` | `0x05` | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | Key released |
 
-### META (0x05)
+### META (0x04)
 
 | Command | Value | A | B | C | Description |
 |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------------|
 | `RESET` | `0x01` | 0 | 0 | 0 | Host must clear all rendered output |
 | `ENVIRONMENT` | `0x02` | viewportWidth (f32) | viewportHeight (f32) | 0 | Viewport size in logical points (host → guest) |
 
 ---
 
 ## Reactive Emission
 
 The engine emits **only what changed** relative to its previous emission:
 
 - **Property diff**: a changed `spacing`/`padding`/text emits a single
   `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` for that node.
 - **Structural diff**: a node added/removed/moved emits the corresponding
   `TREE` opcode(s).
 - **Steady state**: an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes.
 
 Signals in the application drive this: a signal marks the tree dirty; the
 engine's next `emit` reconciles and writes only the delta. The renderer applies
 each frame as a delta to its native elements.
 
 ---
 
 ## Linear Memory Layout
 
 The guest engine and host share a **single linear memory**. Regions are fixed at module start:
 
 ```
 +───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
 | 0x0000  Header block (64 B)  — cursors, frame counter, layout  |
 | 0x0040  Ring buffer (16 B × slotCount)                         |
 | ...      (slots densely packed, 64-byte aligned base)          |
 | 0x10040 Arena (bump region for strings / token paths / lists)  |
 | ...                                                            |
 +───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
 ```
 
 ### Header block (64 bytes)
 
 | Offset | Size | Field | Producer | Description |
 |--------|------|-------|----------|-------------|
 | 0x00 | 4 | `magic` | — | `0x504C504C` (`PLPL`) |
 | 0x04 | 2 | `version` | — | Wire protocol version (1) |
 | 0x06 | 4 | `ringOffset` | — | Byte offset of the ring region |
 | 0x0A | 4 | `ringBytes` | — | Byte length of the ring region |
 | 0x0E | 4 | `slotCount` | — | Number of ring slots (power of two) |
 | 0x12 | 4 | `arenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the arena region |
 | 0x14 | 4 | `arenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the arena region |
 | 0x18 | 4 | `arenaCursor` | guest | Next free byte in the arena |
 | 0x1C | 4 | `readCursor` | host | Ring slot the host has consumed up to |
 | 0x20 | 4 | `writeCursor` | guest | Ring slot the guest has written up to |
 | 0x24 | 4 | `frameCount` | guest | Monotonic completed-frame counter |
 | 0x28 | 36 | reserved | — | Zero |
 
 ### Ring buffer
 
 - Contiguous array of **16-byte slots**; `slotCount` is a **power of two** (wrap via mask, no modulo).
 - **Producer** (guest) writes at `writeCursor`, then advances `writeCursor` and increments `frameCount` at frame end.
 - **Consumer** (host) reads from `readCursor` up to `writeCursor`; after draining a frame it advances `readCursor`.
 - **Backpressure**: the producer must not advance `writeCursor` past `readCursor` (ring full). The producer SHOULD flush a frame before the ring is full.
 - **Frame boundary detection**: the host watches `frameCount`. When it advances, exactly one frame (all slots from the previously consumed `readCursor` to the current `writeCursor`) is complete.
 
 ### Arena
 
 - A pre-allocated **bump region** for variable-length data (strings, token paths).
 - Every arena entry is **self-describing**: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`.
 - Opcodes reference entries by their **byte offset** (`arenaRef`), so an entry's length is read directly from the arena — all opcodes stay 16 bytes.
 - The guest advances `arenaCursor` monotonically (no free-list, no fragmentation). The arena MAY be reset via `META::RESET`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Colors
 
 Literal colors are **sRGB** (IEC 61966-2-1, D65 white point), packed as `0xAARRGGBB`:
 
 - `AA`: alpha (0x00 transparent – 0xFF opaque)
 - `RR`: red, `GG`: green, `BB`: blue
 
 Stored little-endian in a `u32` payload. Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation remain **renderer-owned** (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)).
 
 ---
 
 ## Design Token System
 
 ### Core Principle
 
 > **The renderer owns the defaults. The application owns the overrides.**
 
 This ensures a native look-and-feel by default and cross-platform consistency when the application overrides tokens.
 
 ### Responsibilities
 
 | Aspect | Owner | Responsibility |
 |--------|-------|----------------|
 | **Default Token Values** | Renderer | Define platform-appropriate defaults for all standard tokens |
 | **Token Overrides** | Application | Specify overrides for cross-platform consistency |
 | **Token Resolution** | Renderer | Resolve final token values (override or default) |
 | **Platform Adaptation** | Renderer | Adapt default token values to platform conventions |
 
 ### Token Identification
 
 Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`, `font.body`), case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. The `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) references a token path stored in the arena; `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides a token's value globally.
 
 ### Token Resolution Algorithm
 
 ```
 FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath: string) -> PropertyValue:
     IF applicationOverrides.has(tokenPath):
         RETURN applicationOverrides[tokenPath]
     ELSE IF rendererDefaults.has(tokenPath):
         RETURN rendererDefaults[tokenPath]
     ELSE IF hasParentToken(tokenPath):
         RETURN resolveToken(getParentPath(tokenPath))
     ELSE:
         RETURN getFallbackValue(tokenPath)
 ```
 
 ### Renderer Responsibilities
 
 The renderer MUST:
 
 1. Provide platform-appropriate defaults for all standard tokens (e.g. `color.primary`, `font.body.size`, `space.md`).
 2. Accept `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides.
 3. Resolve design-token references in properties.
 4. Fall back to defaults when no override exists.
 5. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.
 
 The application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` and reference tokens via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; it MUST NOT assume specific default token values.
 
 ### Standard Token Catalog
 
 Required core tokens (renderer MUST support with platform-appropriate defaults): `color.primary`, `color.secondary`, `color.background`, `color.surface`, `color.text.primary`, `color.text.secondary`, `color.border`, `font.body.size`, `font.body.weight`, `font.body.family`, `space.xs`–`space.lg`.
 
 Recommended extended tokens: `color.success`, `color.warning`, `color.danger`, `color.info`, `font.heading.1`–`font.heading.6`, `font.size.heading.1`–`6`, `radius.sm`/`md`, `elevation.low`/`high`, `opacity.disabled`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Frame Lifecycle
 
 A frame is a batch of delta opcodes produced by one `emit` pass:
 
 1. Guest begins a frame.
 2. Guest emits the delta opcodes (tree structure and/or property changes) into consecutive ring slots.
 3. Guest allocates strings in the arena as needed.
 4. Guest `end_frame()`: publishes `writeCursor`, then increments `frameCount`.
 5. Host observes `frameCount` change, drains `[readCursor, writeCursor)`, advances `readCursor`.
 
 Because the ring and arena are plain memory, the guest publishes via a single release store of `frameCount`; the host acquires on read.
 
 ---
 
 ## Conformance
 
 Golden byte vectors for this protocol are in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md).

## Category Table

| Category | Value | Name | Producer | Description |

| `STYLE` | `0x02` | Constraints & tokens | Guest engine | Property values (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |

## Command Tables

### TREE (0x01)

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `CREATE_NODE` | `0x01` | nodeId | componentType (u16, low) | 0 | — | Create a node of `componentType` |
| `DELETE_NODE` | `0x02` | nodeId | 0 | 0 | — | Delete a node and its subtree |
| `INSERT_CHILD` | `0x03` | parentId | childId | index | `0x0001` = append | Insert `childId` into `parentId` at `index` |
| `REMOVE_CHILD` | `0x04` | parentId | childId | 0 | — | Remove `childId` from `parentId` |
| `MOVE_CHILD` | `0x05` | parentId | childId | newIndex | `0x0001` = append | Move child to `newIndex` (after removal) |

### STYLE (0x02)

The engine does not emit positions. `STYLE` carries the **constraint properties**
that native renderers feed to their own layout — spacing, padding, alignment,
FILL/HUG size hints, colors, fonts.

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `SET_PROPERTY` | `0x01` | nodeId | propertyId (u16, low) + valueType (u8, high byte) | value | — | Set a constraint/style property; `value` depends on `valueType` |
| `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x02` | arenaRef (path) | valueType (u8) | value | — | Override a design token; path is an arena string |
| `SET_TEXT` | `0x03` | nodeId | arenaRef (utf8) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content |

`SET_PROPERTY` encodes the value type in the **high byte of `B`** (bits 24–31) and the property id in the low two bytes:

```
B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
```

#### Value types

| Value Type | Value | C / value encoding |
|------------|-------|--------------------|
| `U8` | `0x01` | low byte of C |
| `U32` | `0x02` | u32 |
| `I32` | `0x03` | i32 |
| `F32` | `0x04` | f32 |
| `STRING` | `0x05` | arenaRef (utf8) |
| `ENUM` | `0x06` | low byte of C |
| `COLOR` | `0x07` | packed `0xAARRGGBB` |
| `DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x08` | arenaRef (token path) |

#### Constraint properties for native layout

The following properties drive native layout; the renderer maps them to its
native equivalents (e.g. `SPACING` → GTK box spacing / CSS `gap`, `PADDING` →
widget margin / CSS `padding`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` → size requests). Special
`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1` = FILL (expand to available), `-2` = HUG_CONTENT
(native intrinsic size).

| Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
|----------|-------|------|----------------|

### EVENT (0x03) — host → guest

Events are the **raw inputs**: the renderer reports what happened (a pointer
went down/moved/up, a key went down/up) and resolves which node it hit via its
own rendered-output tree. High-level interpretations — tap, drag, long-press —
are built by the guest/app from these raw inputs and are **not** part of the
protocol.

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |

metadata.preview:
**The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
*what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
signals in the application ensure only changed nodes emit opcodes, so an
unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.

## Core Principles

- **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and gestures
- **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode
- **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine emits structure + constraint properties (spacing, padding, alignment); native renderers compute positions
- **Native elements everywhere**: GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent
- **Reactive emission**: only the nodes that changed emit opcodes; steady state emits zero
- **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
- **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
- **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
- **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes
- **Worker-first heritage**: the architecture keeps the application logic separable from rendering, and WASM/WIT makes components consumable from any language

## Documentation

## Core Principles

- **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and gestures

- **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory

## Goal

Implement the **core components and modifiers in Rust** with a SwiftUI-like API. A `View`/builder abstraction that produces a view tree, which the layout engine (`pathland-layout`) turns into LAYOUT opcodes emitted into the 16-byte ring buffer (Goal 1).

All core components must be written in Rust. The API stays SwiftUI-inspired; later goals make these components consumable from other languages via WASM/WIT.

## Scope

New crates in `lib/rust/`:

- **`pathland-view`** — SwiftUI-style DSL skeleton:
  - Components: `VStack`, `HStack`, `Text` (foundation set; more components deferred).
  - Modifiers: `.padding()`, `.spacing()`, `.fontSize()`, `.color()`, `.background()` (foundation set), chainable.
  - A `View` trait / builder so custom views can be composed.
- **`pathland-engine`** — wires view tree →  ring buffer emission.
- Basic unit tests validating bounds math (spacing, padding, alignment, content sizing).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `VStack` / `HStack` / `Text` compose with chainable modifiers in Rust, SwiftUI-style.
- [ ] A minimal tree (e.g. HStack of two Texts with padding/spacing) lays out to correct bounds.
- [ ] `cargo test` green; crates build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- [ ] Public API mirrors the SwiftUI concepts documented in `AGENTS.md`.

## Dependencies

- **Blocks on:** Goal 1 (16-byte opcode engine).
- **Blocks:** Goals 3, 4, 5.

## Plan: POC Goal 2 — Core components & modifiers in Rust (#13)

### 1. New crate `pathland-view` (SwiftUI-faithful DSL)

**Traits & composition (confirmed design):**
- `trait View { fn build(&self) -> Node; }`
- `trait ViewModifier { fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node); }`
- `struct Modified<V, M>` implementing `View` — blanket `.modifier()` on `View`
- Chains nest as `Modified<Modified<Text, Padding>, Background>`; `build()` collapses to a `Node`, applied innermost-first
- **Allow-and-ignore**: any modifier applies to any view; unsupported combos just emit the property and the renderer ignores it

**Core views (builder structs implementing `View`):**
- `VStack::new().children(Vec<Box<dyn View>>)`, `HStack::new()`, `Text::new("...")`
- `build()` assigns stable sequential ids (internal counter, pre-order)

**Core modifiers (structs implementing `ViewModifier`):**
| Modifier | Property | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Spacing(f32)` | SPACING `0x0001` | F32 |
| `Padding(f32)` | PADDING `0x0004` | F32 |
| `FontSize(f32)` | FONT_SIZE `0x1007` | F32 |
| `Color(u32)` | COLOR `0x100A` | COLOR (0x07) |
| `Background(u32)` | BACKGROUND_COLOR `0x1001` | COLOR (0x07) |

**Sugar (confirmed):** convenience methods on `View` — `.spacing(v)`, `.padding(v)`, `.font_size(v)`, `.color(c)`, `.background(c)` → each returns `Modified<Self, M>`. `.modifier(Custom)` remains for app-defined modifiers.

**Custom modifiers (confirmed):** app structs implement `ViewModifier` and compose by calling core modifiers inside `apply()`:

```rust
struct Card;
impl ViewModifier for Card {
    fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
        Padding(16.0).apply(node);
        Background(0xFF_EEEEEE).apply(node);
    }
}
```

- **Steady state**: unchanged tree still emits zero (existing engine invariant preserved).
